metadata.Title tag: Bedroom Closet Systems, Walk-In and Reach-In | Organized Living
metadata.Meta description: Bedroom closet systems from Organized Living: adjustable freedomRail, built-in Select and Classica, fixed laminate VUE, and ventilated wire shelving.

changes.original: Walk-In and Reach-In Systems in Wood, Laminate and Ventilated Wire
changes.implemented: Walk-In and Reach-In Systems in Laminate and Ventilated Wire

changes.original: Organized Living manufactures bedroom closet systems in three construction families: modular rail shelving that adjusts without tools, built-in wood and laminate systems finished like cabinetry, and fixed ventilated wire that brackets straight to the wall. Each one combines hanging rods, shelves, baskets and drawers to hold a wardrobe in the space a bedroom actually gives it, whether that is a reach-in behind a pair of doors or a walk-in you stand inside. We have built storage systems since 1919 and make them at a 680,000 square foot facility in Bloomington, Indiana, where the load ratings are tested: Lifetime ventilated wire carries up to 75 pounds per linear foot and Shelftech up to 45. Orders ship across the United States and Canada in 3 to 5 business days.
changes.implemented: Organized Living manufactures bedroom closet systems in three construction families: modular rail shelving that adjusts after installation, built-in laminate systems finished like cabinetry, and fixed ventilated wire that mounts directly to the wall. Our hanging rods, shelves, baskets and drawers organize wardrobes in reach-in closets and walk-in dressing rooms. Lifetime ventilated wire supports up to 75 pounds per linear foot and Shelftech up to 45 when installed according to the applicable instructions.

changes.original: Three construction families cover a bedroom closet, and the one you pick decides how the closet behaves in five years rather than how it photographs on day one. A modular system hangs its shelves from a rail and moves whenever the wardrobe changes. A built-in fixes everything in position and reads as cabinetry. Fixed ventilated wire brackets to the studs and carries the most weight per foot.
changes.implemented: Three construction families cover a bedroom closet. A modular system supports shelves and rods on an adjustable rail. Built-in laminate creates a cabinet finish, while fixed ventilated wire mounts directly to the wall. The choice determines how the layout can change as the wardrobe changes.

changes.original: Modular systems suspend each shelf and rod from one horizontal rail, so a hanging section becomes a shelf section without patching drywall. A wardrobe is the most changeable thing a house stores, which is what makes adjustability worth more in a bedroom than anywhere else.
changes.implemented: Modular systems support shelves and rods on uprights suspended from a horizontal rail. Once installed, compatible components can be moved without patching drywall, so a hanging section can become a shelf section as storage needs change.

changes.original: freedomRail is the adjustable rail system, built around uprights that hook onto a single wall-mounted rail. Rods, shelves, baskets and hooks slide along it and lift out at any height, so a double-hang section converts to long-hang for coats in minutes.
changes.implemented: freedomRail is our adjustable rail system, built around uprights that hook onto a single wall-mounted rail. Compatible rods, shelves, baskets and hooks reposition on the uprights, so a double-hang section can convert to long-hang for dresses and coats.

changes.original: freedomRail EDGE adds a finished front edge to the same rail platform. It earns its place in a walk-in, where the shelf profile is on view from inside the room rather than hidden behind a closed door.
changes.implemented: freedomRail EDGE serves garage and household gear storage. Our freedomRail collection provides adjustable hanging, shelving and closet accessories for bedroom wardrobes.

changes.original: Built-In Bedroom Closet Systems
changes.implemented: Built-In and Fixed Laminate Bedroom Systems

changes.original: Built-in systems fix their shelves and drawer boxes in place, trading adjustability for a cabinet finish. In a walk-in that functions as a dressing room, that trade is usually the right one.
changes.implemented: Laminate systems create a coordinated cabinet appearance in reach-in closets and walk-in dressing rooms. Select and Classica offer built-in storage, while VUE provides fixed solid shelving. Adjustment and accessory options depend on the collection.

changes.original: Select is the laminate built-in line, assembled from fixed panels and shelves across a range of finishes. Drawers and doors come as part of the line, which answers the bedroom closet that needs to hide folded knitwear and accessories rather than display them.
changes.implemented: Select combines fixed panels with movable shelving and compatible drawers for a built-in appearance. Doors and drawers provide closed storage for folded knitwear and bedroom accessories.

changes.original: Classica carries moulding and raised panel detail for a closet that continues the trim language of the bedroom around it. In an older house with deep skirting and panelled doors, flat slab fronts sit wrong against the existing joinery.
changes.implemented: Classica combines furniture-grade laminate with coordinated door and drawer styles, moulding options and soft-close glides. The collection supports a finished dressing-room appearance that can complement the bedroom trim and cabinetry.

changes.original: VUE is the wood built-in line, and it earns its place when a walk-in has no door at all. Shelf faces and finishes are made to be looked at, which is what an open dressing area demands.
changes.implemented: VUE combines fixed thermally fused laminate shelving with concealed hardware for a clean, coordinated closet. Shelf towers and compatible drawers expand storage options.

changes.original: Fixed ventilated shelving brackets directly to studs and does not move once installed, which buys the highest load rating in the range. Air moves through it, and a closed bedroom closet holding worn garments generates no airflow of its own.
changes.implemented: Fixed ventilated shelving mounts directly to the wall with the specified brackets and hardware. Open wire leaves space for air to circulate around stored clothing.

changes.original: Lifetime ventilated wire supports up to 75 pounds per linear foot, the highest published figure we make. A shelf run carrying folded denim and boxed footwear loads closer to that number than a rod of shirts ever will.
changes.implemented: Lifetime ventilated wire supports up to 75 pounds per linear foot when properly installed. Shelf-and-hang and shelving options provide storage for clothing, folded garments and boxed footwear.

changes.original: Shelftech supports up to 45 pounds per linear foot and uses a tighter wire spacing than standard shelving. Closer spacing stops small items tipping through, which matters on the shoe shelf more than anywhere else in a bedroom.
changes.implemented: Shelftech is our economical fixed ventilated wire option, supporting up to 45 pounds per linear foot when properly installed. Shelving and hanging configurations suit bedroom storage and repeatable construction layouts.

changes.original: Two closet shapes account for almost every bedroom, and they are not the same problem scaled up and down. A reach-in is a wall you fit out and view from outside. A walk-in is a small room you stand inside, which changes where things go, how the corners behave and whether the shelf faces are on show.
changes.implemented: A reach-in is fitted along a wall and accessed from outside. A walk-in is a small room with space to stand inside. That distinction changes the circulation, treatment of corners and visibility of shelf faces.

changes.original: A reach-in gives you one usable wall and roughly 24 inches of depth, so every inch of height has to work. Double-hang doubles the rod capacity of the same footprint, and the shelf above the top rod is the only place bulky seasonal items fit. The doors set the limit: anything stored in the corners behind a bi-fold sits in a blind zone, which is what pull-out baskets are for.
changes.implemented: A reach-in commonly has about 24 inches of depth. Double-hang adds a second rod within the same wall run, while upper shelves hold boxed seasonal items. Door openings and blind corners determine which shelves, drawers and compatible pull-out baskets remain accessible.

changes.original: A walk-in has three or four walls and a floor you occupy, so the design question shifts from capacity to circulation. Keep a clear path of at least 24 inches and treat the corners deliberately, because two runs meeting at 90 degrees either lose a foot of hanging space or need a dedicated corner unit. An island suits a walk-in wider than roughly 10 feet and becomes an obstacle in anything narrower.
changes.implemented: A walk-in provides storage along multiple walls and a floor area for circulation. Plan the corners, open drawers and clear walking space together. An island adds storage only when the room has enough clearance around each side in use.

changes.original: Rod height is the single biggest capacity decision in a bedroom closet. One rod at 84 inches wastes the wall beneath it; two rods at 42 and 84 double the capacity of the same run for shirts, folded trousers and jackets. Long-hang stays for dresses and coats, and it only needs one section rather than a whole wall.
changes.implemented: Double-hang adds a second rod within the same wall run for shirts, folded trousers and jackets. Our Bedroom Storage 101 guide illustrates rod heights around 42 and 84 inches for an 8-foot ceiling. A separate long-hang section accommodates dresses and coats; final heights depend on garment length and reach.

changes.original: Folded garments and footwear load a shelf harder per foot than anything hanging, which is why the ventilated lines carry them. Ventilated wire also keeps air moving around clothing that has been worn, in a space that is closed most of the day.
changes.implemented: Shelves hold folded knitwear, denim and footwear in separate groups. Open wire leaves space for air to circulate around stored items, while solid shelving supports a continuous surface. Shelf spacing and load limits depend on the selected system.

changes.original: Small items that will not stack belong in drawers: watches, belts, jewellery and folded underwear. Soft-close glides stop a loaded drawer slamming, which matters in a closet that shares a wall with the bed.
changes.implemented: Small items that will not stack belong in drawers: watches, belts, jewelry and folded underwear. Selected drawer configurations offer soft-close glides for controlled closing. Drawer and insert compatibility depends on the product line.

changes.original: Pull-out baskets convert the unreachable back of a deep shelf into storage by bringing the contents forward. Hooks and valet rods claim the door back and the gap beneath the lowest shelf, taking robes and next-day outfits off the shelf stack entirely.
changes.implemented: Compatible pull-out baskets bring contents forward for access. Hooks, valet rods and dedicated over-the-door organizers provide separate places for robes, bags and next-day outfits. Each accessory needs the mounting components specified in its product listing.

changes.original: Finishes run across wood tones, neutral greys and metal hardware, so a closet either matches the bedroom's millwork or disappears against it. Chocolate Pear gives the warm wood tone, Century Gray and Slate cover the cool neutrals, White stays the default for a reach-in that should recede, and Chrome and Nickel finish the rods and brackets. Every finish reference is listed on the specification sheet for its line.
changes.implemented: Our finishes run across wood tones, neutral greys and metal hardware. Chocolate Pear provides a warm wood tone, Century Gray and Slate cover cool neutrals, and White creates a light backdrop for a reach-in. Chrome and Nickel are available on selected hardware. Finish and hardware availability varies by collection and component.

changes.original: Bedroom closet organization starts with the shape of the opening, not the size of the wardrobe. Seven layouts cover almost every bedroom, and the shape decides the system before taste gets a say.
changes.implemented: Bedroom closet organization starts with the opening, usable walls and wardrobe. Seven layout approaches arrange long-hang, double-hang, folded clothing and drawers around those constraints.

changes.original: In a small reach-in the winning move is double-hang plus a single top shelf, not a wider rod. Tight rod spacing at 42 inches suits shirts and folded trousers, and it turns one wall into two.
changes.implemented: A small reach-in can combine double-hang with a top shelf. Two rod levels use the wall height for shirts and folded trousers, while upper shelving holds less frequently used items. Rod spacing must suit the ceiling, garment lengths and reach.

changes.original: Below roughly 6 feet across, a walk-in works as a single-sided or L-shaped run rather than a facing pair, because two opposing runs leave no room to turn with a drawer open.
changes.implemented: A small walk-in can use a single-sided or L-shaped run. Measure the depth of hanging clothes and the space needed to open drawers before adding storage on an opposing wall.

changes.original: A U-shape uses three walls and produces two inside corners, each of which either loses hanging space or takes a corner unit. Plan the corners first and the rest of the run follows.
changes.implemented: A U-shape uses three walls and creates two inside corners. Plan how hanging rods, shelves and drawers meet at those corners before filling the remaining wall runs.

changes.original: An island adds drawer capacity and a folding surface, and it needs at least 36 inches of clearance on every side it is used from. That puts the practical minimum room width at around 10 feet.
changes.implemented: An island adds drawer capacity and a folding surface. Its size must allow circulation and full drawer extension around every side in use. Room width alone does not determine whether an island fits.

changes.original: Measure your own closet before ordering. The figures below are planning guidance from the wider market rather than our own specifications, and shelf dimensions for each product line are published on its specification sheet.
changes.implemented: Measure the closet before ordering. The dimensions below are planning examples from our Bedroom Storage 101 guide, not universal installation requirements. Product specification sheets provide the dimensions and mounting requirements for each system.

changes.original: Rod height is where a reach-in is won or lost. A single rod at 84 inches leaves most of the wall doing nothing, and the fix costs one extra rod rather than a bigger closet.
changes.implemented: Double-hang can increase hanging capacity without enlarging the closet. Measure shirts, folded trousers, jackets and long garments before setting the two rod levels.

changes.original: Get the depth right and the rest forgives you. Past roughly 26 inches nobody reaches the back of a shelf, and a pull-out basket starts paying for itself against a deeper one.
changes.implemented: Account for the depth of shelves, hanging garments and accessories, plus the door opening and drawer extension. A deeper shelf is useful only when its contents remain accessible.

changes.original: freedomRail Closet Kits. Complete adjustable kits sized for a closet run, with rail, uprights, rods, shelves and brackets supplied together.  https://shop.organizedliving.com/freedomrail/freedomrail-closet-kits
changes.implemented: Complete adjustable kits for a closet run, with included components listed on each kit page.

changes.original: Shelves, Brackets and Rods. Individual ventilated shelves, brackets and hanging rods for extending or rebuilding an existing closet.  https://shop.organizedliving.com/freedomrail/freedomrail-shelves-brackets-rods
changes.implemented: Individual shelves, brackets and hanging rods for extending or rebuilding a compatible freedomRail closet.

changes.original: Baskets and Accessories. Pull-out baskets, hooks and valet rods that mount to the same systems.  https://shop.organizedliving.com/freedomrail/freedomrail-accessories
changes.implemented: Compatible baskets, hooks, valet rods and organizers. Check each product listing for required mounting components.

changes.original: Over the Door Storage. Door-back racks that claim the vertical space a shelf run leaves behind, useful in a reach-in.  https://shop.organizedliving.com/over-the-door
changes.implemented: Door-back organizers add vertical storage beyond the main shelf run. Check door fit and clearance before ordering.

changes.original: Build Your Own Bedroom Closet With the Design Tool
changes.implemented: Design a Bedroom Closet With Our Design Tool

changes.original: The Design Tool generates a bedroom closet design from your measurements and your chosen product line, and returns a configuration ready to order. Enter the dimensions, pick a family, and it produces the rod and shelf layout rather than leaving you to work it out from a parts list. The shop answers questions during ordering, and an Installing Dealer picks up a designed project from there.
changes.implemented: Our Design Tool supports room measurements, finish selection and drag-and-drop shelves, rods and accessories. Completed designs can be saved, shared and purchased through our shop. An Installing Dealer can help plan layouts outside the tool’s supported room geometry.

changes.original: Who installs it decides which of the two routes you take. Order a kit direct and fit it over a weekend, or hand the measuring, ordering and installing to a Dealer. Products ship throughout the United States and Canada, generally in 3 to 5 business days from the warehouse, with timing varying by product, order size, destination and delivery method.
changes.implemented: Order a DIY system through our shop or work with an Installing Dealer for measuring, design and installation. Our online shop ships within the contiguous United States. Items generally leave the Bloomington facility in 3 to 5 business days, with transit time varying by shipment and destination. Installing Dealers serve projects across the U.S. and Canada.

changes.original: Buying direct suits a reach-in where the measurements are simple and the fit is a weekend job. Orders arrive in job boxes built for handling on site, each carrying a QR code that links to the installation information for what is inside. PayPal Pay Later is available at the shop checkout.
changes.implemented: freedomRail and Select support DIY installation. Our installation library provides product-specific guides and videos for planning the work, identifying mounting hardware and assembling compatible components. Current availability and checkout options appear in the shop.

changes.original: An Installing Dealer handles measurement, ordering and installation, which suits a walk-in, an island or any closet whose walls are not square. We build the systems and the dealer network fits them, so the Dealer Locator leads to an installed closet instead of a boxed kit.
changes.implemented: An Installing Dealer handles measurement, ordering and installation for reach-ins, walk-ins and dressing-room projects. Organized Living manufactures the systems, and our dealer network provides installation services.

changes.original: Homeowners reach a finished closet fastest. Draw it in the Design Tool, then either check out through the shop or carry that design to a local Installing Dealer.
changes.implemented: Plan a bedroom closet in our Design Tool, then order through the shop or discuss the design with a local Installing Dealer.

changes.original: Specifying by the unit rather than one closet at a time moves the priority from finish to repeatability and schedule. Ventilated wire installs quickly after drywall and paint, and we support programme selection and pricing at that scale through our sales team.
changes.implemented: Multi-unit bedroom storage prioritizes repeatable layouts, specifications and installation schedules. Our ventilated wire supports installation after drywall and paint, and our sales team supports product selection for single-family and multifamily projects.

changes.original: Architects want the numbers, not the narrative. Every line documents its load ratings, material content and finish specifications, and each downloads straight into a project file.
changes.implemented: Product brochures, statements of line and specification sheets document system dimensions, materials and finishes. Our published resources support product selection and project documentation.

changes.original: Why Choose Organized Living for Your Bedroom Closet
changes.implemented: Why Choose Organized Living for a Bedroom Closet

changes.original: Four of the five reasons below are specific to a bedroom wardrobe rather than to closets generally, because clothing loads a system differently from anything else a house stores.
changes.implemented: Our bedroom storage range combines published shelving capacities, adjustable configurations and finishes for reach-in closets and walk-in dressing rooms.

changes.original: Rod and Shelf Rated for a Full Wardrobe
changes.implemented: Published Shelving Capacities

changes.original: A packed double-hang run and a shelf of boxed footwear are the two heaviest things in a bedroom closet. The published ratings are sized for that: 75 pounds per linear foot on Lifetime ventilated wire, 45 on Shelftech, both from testing rather than from the design drawing.
changes.implemented: Lifetime ventilated wire supports up to 75 pounds per linear foot and Shelftech up to 45 when properly installed. The selected system’s specifications determine the required supports, spacing and loading conditions.

changes.original: Ventilated wire moves air around garments inside a closed closet, which a solid shelf cannot manage. That is why wire remains standard in clothing storage long after it was replaced elsewhere in the house.
changes.implemented: Open wire shelving leaves space for air to circulate around stored clothing. Ventilated shelves provide an alternative to solid shelving for folded garments, footwear and other bedroom items.

changes.original: Suits, dresses and folded knitwear each need a different clearance, and a rail system holds all three without settling on a compromise height. Spacing changes as the wardrobe changes, with no new holes in the wall.
changes.implemented: Suits, dresses and folded knitwear need different clearances. After installation, compatible freedomRail components reposition on the existing rail and uprights as the wardrobe changes.

changes.original: Built for Reach-In Depths, Not Just Walk-Ins
changes.implemented: Storage for Reach-Ins and Walk-Ins

changes.original: Most bedrooms have a reach-in, not a dressing room, and the range is built for the depths they actually are. Shelf and bracket sizes cover the shallow run rather than assuming the dimensions of a walk-in.
changes.implemented: Our range includes shelf, rod and accessory configurations for reach-in openings and walk-in rooms. Planning starts with usable wall dimensions, door access and the clothing to be stored.

changes.original: Manufactured in Bloomington Since 1919
changes.implemented: Manufacturing Experience Since 1919

changes.original: We have built storage systems since 1919 and remain third-generation family owned. Production runs from a 680,000 square foot facility in Bloomington, Indiana, which is also where the testing happens.
changes.implemented: Organized Living traces its manufacturing history to 1919. Our ventilated shelving line launched in 1976, and our manufacturing and distribution operations include the 680,000-square-foot facility in Bloomington, Indiana.

changes.original: The rod and shelf ratings quoted above came off a test rig in Bloomington, Indiana, not off a design drawing. Four steps run from raw steel to the published figure.
changes.implemented: Materials, finishes and installation details work together to support the published product specifications. Our product documents provide the requirements for selecting and installing each bedroom closet system.

changes.original: 01  Material  Steel is 95 to 97 percent recycled. Laminate is 90 to 100 percent post-industrial recovered, plus 5 percent post-consumer.
changes.implemented: Our steel contains recycled material, and our thermally fused laminate incorporates recovered wood content. Published sustainability information describes the materials used across the range.

changes.original: 02  Coating  A proprietary epoxy powder hybrid, applied by a process designed to produce zero waste and zero VOC release.
changes.implemented: Our ventilated wire uses an epoxy powder coating. Published sustainability information describes the coating process and its approach to material recovery and emissions.

changes.original: 03  Testing  Load capacity, durability and performance are measured in-house, at the 680,000 square foot plant that builds them.
changes.implemented: Support spacing, mounting hardware and installation details affect performance. Each system must follow its own published installation requirements.

changes.original: 04  Published  75 and 45 lbs per linear foot on Lifetime ventilated wire and Shelftech. Warranty terms are published per line.
changes.implemented: Lifetime and Shelftech publish capacities of up to 75 and 45 pounds per linear foot respectively. Other systems have their own specifications and installation conditions.

changes.original: Three downloads sit on every product line's own page: a brochure, a statement of line and a data specification sheet. Between them they hold the dimensions, load figures and finish references an architect needs to specify a system in project documents. Warranty terms sit separately, on our support page.
changes.implemented: Our product pages provide brochures, statements of line and specification sheets, with available documents varying by collection. These resources cover dimensions, materials and finishes. The applicable written warranty provides coverage terms and the claim process.

changes.original: A&E, HGTV and PBS have all filmed our systems, and home titles including Better Homes & Gardens have published them.
changes.implemented: Organized Living has been featured by A&E, HGTV, PBS and Better Homes & Gardens.

changes.original: Who builds this, what people ask before they buy, and the guides worth reading while the tape measure is still out.
changes.implemented: Company information, buying answers and bedroom planning guides in one place.

changes.original: Organized Living manufactures home storage and closet organization systems and sells them through a nationwide dealer network and a direct shop. We were founded in 1919 in Norwood, Ohio, remain third-generation family owned, and build at a 680,000 square foot facility in Bloomington, Indiana. We manufacture; we do not install. That is why a system reaches you through a Dealer or the shop instead of a crew of ours.
changes.implemented: Organized Living manufactures home storage and closet organization systems, available through a dealer network and a direct shop. Our company began in 1919 in Norwood, Ohio, and our ventilated shelving line launched in 1976. Manufacturing and distribution operations include our 680,000-square-foot Bloomington, Indiana, facility. Installation is provided by Installing Dealers or completed as a DIY project.

changes.original: Generally 3 to 5 business days for products available from the warehouse. Actual timing varies by product, order size, destination and delivery method.
changes.implemented: Items generally ship from our Bloomington facility in 3 to 5 business days. This is dispatch timing; delivery also depends on transit time. Our online shop ships within the contiguous United States. Availability, order size and destination affect the schedule.

changes.original: Baskets, drawers, hooks, valet rods and shelf accessories all mount to the same systems, and components mix across the product lines.
changes.implemented: Accessory compatibility depends on the product line and mounting component. For example, OBoxes mount to freedomRail Uprights, while the OBox Chrome Basket with Glide requires an OBox 1-Shelf Unit. Product listings identify the required host and spacing.

changes.original: A reach-in is a single fitted wall you view from outside, usually around 24 inches deep. A walk-in is a small room you stand inside, which adds corners, circulation and visible shelf faces.
changes.implemented: A reach-in is accessed from outside the closet, commonly with about 24 inches of depth. A walk-in provides space to stand inside, so corners, circulation and visible shelf faces become part of the layout.

changes.original: 24 inches suits a reach-in, which is enough for a hanger to sit square to the wall. Past roughly 26 inches the back of a shelf stops being reachable without pull-out baskets.
changes.implemented: About 24 inches is a common planning depth for a reach-in, as shown in our Bedroom Storage 101 guide. Confirm hanger depth, doors, trim and the selected components before ordering.

changes.original: Around 42 and 84 inches. That carries shirts, folded trousers and jackets on both levels and doubles the capacity of the same wall.
changes.implemented: Our Bedroom Storage 101 guide illustrates approximately 42 and 84 inches for double-hang rods under a 96-inch ceiling. Adjust the layout to garment length, available height and reach.

changes.original: Lifetime ventilated shelving supports up to 75 pounds per linear foot, and Shelftech up to 45 pounds per linear foot. Both ratings are published on this site.
changes.implemented: Lifetime ventilated shelving supports up to 75 pounds per linear foot and Shelftech up to 45 when properly installed. Capacity varies by system, support spacing and mounting conditions; use the applicable specification sheet.

changes.original: Yes. Kits ship in job boxes with a QR code linking to the installation information for the parts inside.
changes.implemented: freedomRail and Select support DIY installation. Our installation library provides product-specific instructions and videos. Follow the selected system’s mounting and assembly requirements.

changes.original: No. We manufacture the systems, and installation is handled by our Installing Dealer network.
changes.implemented: Organized Living manufactures the systems. Installation is handled by our Installing Dealer network or completed as a DIY project.

changes.original: Terms differ by product line and publish at organizedliving.com/support. Damaged parts are exchanged, and in-warranty failures have all parts replaced.
changes.implemented: Coverage depends on the product line, use and installation. The applicable written warranty sets the terms, exclusions and claim process. Current documents are available through our support resources.

changes.original: Can a system be installed after paint without delays?
changes.implemented: Can shelving be installed after drywall and paint?

changes.original: Yes. Ventilated wire installs quickly after drywall and paint, which is why it suits new construction schedules.
changes.implemented: Our ventilated shelving is designed for installation after drywall and paint. Project timing depends on site readiness and the installation plan.
